_why: Mutant ids declared BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING for RefSpeedExclusion, each with the reason. `vit_mutate.py --equivalences` reads the KEYS of this object, so the reasons live in the same file as the claim and a declared mutant leaves the denominator. THREE are declared, and nothing is declared `unreachable`. That split is the whole story of this unit: the FIRST sweep left EIGHT survivors at 0.7778 (mutation/RefSpeedExclusion.undeclared.json), five of which sat on the exclusion band's edges and its two `/ 2` literals. None of those five was declared. They were KILLED, by repairing the corpus -- `evidence/RefSpeedExclusion/inputs_census.txt` showed `CntrPar%WE_GearboxRatio == 0.0` in 3,027 of 3,967 cases, so three quarters of the corpus divided by zero and every band comparison answered FALSE on both sides identically. Three `values` pins in harness/ranges.toml put the band's edges on rungs `VS_RefSpd`'s own R6 ladder already contained, and the second undeclared sweep (mutation/RefSpeedExclusion.undeclared2.json) killed all five with nothing declared: 33 of 36, 0.9167. The three below are what is left, and each of them is a claim about the PROGRAMS rather than about the corpus. EACH ONE HAS A SIBLING ON THE SAME EXPRESSION THAT IS KILLED, which is the control the campaign asks for (unit #57's rule: an equivalence is declared per mutant, and the proof is that its sibling is not declared).
fa704b00: compare_op '>' -> '>=' at `if (LocalVar->FA_Hist > 0)` on line 96 -- the test INSIDE the `IF (LocalVar%restart)` initialisation block, ControllerBlocks.f90:791 in the clean source. `LocalVar%FA_Hist` is assigned 0 or 1 unconditionally by the two arms of the band test immediately above (lines 73 and 76) and nothing writes it in between, so at this site it is 0 or 1 and `> 0` is exactly `== 1` while `>= 0` is always TRUE. On FA_Hist == 1 the two programs take the same branch and are identical. On FA_Hist == 0 the reference stores `VS_RefSpeed_LSS` into `TRA_LastRefSpd` and the mutant stores `TRA_ExclSpeed +/- TRA_ExclBand/2` instead -- AND THAT VALUE IS THEN DISCARDED WITHOUT BEING READ. The next statement that reads anything is `IF (LocalVar%FA_Hist > 0)` at line 134, which is FALSE (FA_Hist is still 0), so `VS_RefSpd_TRA = VS_RefSpeed_LSS` on both sides; and the unconditional `LocalVar%TRA_LastRefSpd = LocalVar%VS_RefSpd_TRA` below it overwrites the slot with that same value on both sides. `TRA_LastRefSpd` is read exactly once between the two writes, in the branch of line 134 that is not taken. So every compared output -- FA_Hist, TRA_LastRefSpd, VS_RefSpd_TRA, VS_RefSpd_RL, VS_RefSpd, rlP and instRL -- is bit-identical on every admissible input. THE CONTROL: `22e92983` is the SAME operator on the SAME text `if (LocalVar->FA_Hist > 0)` at line 134, and it is KILLED on 2,810 of 13,777 cases. Two identical predicates, one dead and one live, and only the dead one is declared. This is the same shape unit #46 measured from the other side -- an initialisation arm whose two branches reach the same answer -- and the harness's own `no-restart-init` stub measures the size of the live part at 29 cases of 3,967 on the first corpus.
1a7bfcb8: const_tweak '1' -> '2' at `LocalVar->restart ? 1 : 0` in the `ratelimit_c` call, line 172 -- the TRUE arm of the LOGICAL-to-C-int conversion. `ratelimit`'s `reset` dummy is tested for TRUTH and never for a particular value, and it is tested that way in BOTH configurations this campaign builds. Pre-integration the generated bridge converts it back: `refspeedexclusion_callees.f90:28` calls `ratelimit(..., (reset /= 0), ...)`, so 2 and 1 are the same Fortran `.TRUE.`. Post-integration the C++ `ratelimit` receives it directly and `translations/Functions/ratelimit.cpp` tests `if (reset != 0)`, with a comment recording why it must be `!= 0` and not `== 1` (unit #33 measured an inverted MERGE at 3,112 of 3,532 post-integration cases). So no admissible input can separate 2 from 1 at this argument. THE CONTROL: `502c4a4d` is const_tweak '0' -> '1' on the SAME ternary -- the FALSE arm -- and it is KILLED, because 1 in the false arm makes every non-restart call a reset. The two arms of one expression, one declared and one not.
96d44142: const_tweak '0.0' -> '1.0' at the last argument of the `ratelimit_c` call, line 173 -- the `ResetValue` VALUE slot, whose PRESENCE flag is the `0` immediately before it. `ResetValue` is OPTIONAL in the reference and is not passed at this call site (ControllerBlocks.f90:813 in the clean source lists seven actual arguments, not eight), so VIT's bridge carries presence as a separate flag and the value slot is unread on both sides. Pre-integration the generated bridge branches on it and calls `ratelimit` WITHOUT the argument at all (`refspeedexclusion_callees.f90:30`), so the slot never reaches Fortran. Post-integration `translations/Functions/ratelimit.cpp` reads it only under `if (has_ResetValue != 0)`. THE CONTROL: `0f7554dc` is const_tweak '0' -> '1' on the PRESENCE flag beside it, and it is KILLED -- flipping the flag makes `ResetValue_` the value slot instead of `inputSignal` and changes the reset arm's answer. The flag and the value it guards, one killed and one declared, three characters apart.
